walkthroughs.body_html:
Bonding & Energetics — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Bonding & Energetics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Bonding & Energetics.

mcqs.q: What happens to electrons when sodium reacts with chlorine?
options: Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.
Sodium loses one electron to chlorine; the resulting Na+ and Cl- ions attract electrostatically.
Sodium and chlorine share an electron between them.

mcqs.q: When water boils, what is broken?
options: The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Metal atoms themselves move to carry the current.
Delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice of positive ions, carrying charge.
Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “VSEPR theory”?
options: Shared pair of electrons between two atoms, often between non-metals.
Electron pairs around a central atom repel each other and adopt positions maximising separation.
Attraction between a lattice of positive ions and delocalised electrons.
Unequal sharing of electrons between atoms of different electronegativity, producing δ⁺ and δ⁻ charges.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Covalent bonding”?
options: Attraction between a lattice of positive ions and delocalised electrons.
Shared pair of electrons between two atoms, often between non-metals.
Unequal sharing of electrons between atoms of different electronegativity, producing δ⁺ and δ⁻ charges.
Electron pairs around a central atom repel each other and adopt positions maximising separation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Bond polarity”?
options: Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by electron transfer.
Unequal sharing of electrons between atoms of different electronegativity, producing δ⁺ and δ⁻ charges.
Attraction between a lattice of positive ions and delocalised electrons.
Both shared electrons originate from the same atom, e.g. NH₄⁺.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Metallic bonding”?
options: Both shared electrons originate from the same atom, e.g. NH₄⁺.
Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by electron transfer.
Attraction between a lattice of positive ions and delocalised electrons.
Electron pairs around a central atom repel each other and adopt positions maximising separation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ionic bonding”?
options: Both shared electrons originate from the same atom, e.g. NH₄⁺.
Shared pair of electrons between two atoms, often between non-metals.
Unequal sharing of electrons between atoms of different electronegativity, producing δ⁺ and δ⁻ charges.
Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by electron transfer.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Dative covalent bond”?
options: Electron pairs around a central atom repel each other and adopt positions maximising separation.
Unequal sharing of electrons between atoms of different electronegativity, producing δ⁺ and δ⁻ charges.
Both shared electrons originate from the same atom, e.g. NH₄⁺.
Attraction between a lattice of positive ions and delocalised electrons.
